title: Scaena patch
description: A patch (SPEC §7.3): RFC 6902 ops and semantic ops, applied in order, all or none.

Op.description: One op: RFC 6902's, or a semantic op, which compiles to RFC 6902's.

oneOf.description: Put `value` at `path`: a member of an object (one already there is replaced, in its place), or an item of an array, at an index or at its end (`-`).
Take away what is at `path`.
Replace what is at `path`, which must be there.
`remove` at `from`, then `add` at `path`. A member moved within its object keeps its place: a rename.
`add` at `path` what is at `from`.
Fail the patch unless `path` holds `value` (numbers equal by value: 1 is 1.0).

Pointer.description: A JSON Pointer (RFC 6901): empty, the whole document, or `/`-separated tokens, `~1` for a `/` and `~0` for a `~` inside one.

SemanticOp.description: What an author means, compiled to RFC 6902 against the deck as the ops before it leave it (SPEC §7.3). `state` names the state an op acts in, from it on; without one, an op acts on the node's own properties, its defaults. An op on a node in a state needs the node on screen there.

oneOf.description: A node new to the scene graph, last in its order (painted over the others at its `z`). With `state`, it enters there, `props` its delta in that state.
A node, and everything that names it: its deltas, its exits, its choreography, and its overrides. A container must be emptied first.
A node's id, everywhere it is used: the node keeps its place, its type, and every property, so it stays the same node to tracking and to a morph.
A node already in the scene graph enters in a state, `props` its delta there: one that left comes back.
A node leaves in a state: it exits there, or, if it would enter there, it does not.

A new group, `id`, holding `nodes` where they stand (ADR-0008, ADR-0013). They are children of one container, the slide or a group, as `state` shows them (else as their own `at` places them), and take the group as their container wherever that one is written. A group lays nothing out, so nothing moves. It sits where they sat, at the highest `z` among them (0 for one that sets none), last among what stands there; and it shows in each state that shows one of them in it, and only there.

A group's children taken out to the group's own container where they stand, each keeping its own `z`, and the group gone with everything that names it: its deltas, its exits, its choreography, and its overrides. Its look goes with it.

One property (`kind`), or one key of an object property (`at/in`), set to `value`: in a state, as its delta, or in the node's defaults. `null` takes it away: from the node's defaults, or, in a state, from what the node tracks (SPEC §2.2).

A node's place (ADR-0013), as a drag in an editor moves it: the keys of its `at` that say where it goes (`col`, `row`, `in`, `rect`, `area`, `index`) become those of `at`, and the rest of them go. They are written where the placement lives: in the deck's `overrides` if they set it; else in the latest delta that sets it, from `state` back along what it tracks; else in the node's own `at`. Without `state`, in the node's own unless the overrides set it. Its container (`at.parent`) is part of its placement: the node stays in it unless `at` names another, or `null` for the canvas (PLAN 2.50). What holds it says what places it: the theme's grid places a root or a group's member by cells, slot, or `rect`; a grid container by cells, `area`, or `index`; a stack by `index`; a frame by `rect`.

fork.description: Write it into `state`'s own props, wherever the placement lives now: the node goes there in that state, and in the states that track it as they take the rest of its props, and stays where it was in the others. Refused where the deck's `overrides` place the node, in every state.

format.description: The format shown (ADR-0020): where the node has its own layout there (`formats`), the placement is that layout's `at`, the node's own elsewhere as it was. Where it has none, the placement is the node's own, as without it.

anew.description: With `format`: give the node a layout of its own there, if it has none, placed so.

oneOf.description: A text node's `text`, in a state or in its defaults. `runs` there go, so the text is what shows.

Text typed into a text node where it stands (ADR-0013): the characters from `from` to `to` of its text as `state` shows it (its `text`, or its runs' texts end to end, as the deck's `overrides` leave them) become `text`. Offsets count characters (Unicode scalar values). Runs keep their looks: what is typed takes the look of the run it is typed into, the one before where two meet, and a run the edit leaves with no text goes. It is written where the text lives: in the deck's `overrides` if they set it; else in the latest delta that sets it, from `state` back along what it tracks; else in the node's own. Without `state`, in the node's own unless the overrides set it.

fork.description: Write it into `state`'s own props, wherever the text lives now: it reads so there, and in the states that track it as they take the rest of its props, and as it did in the others. Refused where the deck's `overrides` set the text, in every state.

oneOf.description: The look of characters selected in a text node (ADR-0013, PLAN 2.38): characters `from` to `to` of its text as `state` shows it, counted as `replace_text` counts them, take each key of `look`: a run's `role`, `emphasis`, or `lang`, or one key of its `style` (`style/weight`, `style/color`); a key set to `null` is taken away, so the node's own look shows there. The text becomes runs split at `from` and `to`; neighbors left alike are joined, and runs that all read as the node does are its `text` again. It is written where the text lives, as `replace_text` writes typing. A size, and a color written out, are refused: a size comes with a role, and a run takes the theme's names.

fork.description: Write it into `state`'s own props, wherever the text lives now, as `replace_text`'s `fork` does.

oneOf.description: A text's paragraphs as a list's items (ADR-0018, PLAN 2.69): each paragraph characters `from` to `to` of its text touch, counted as `replace_text` counts them, set to `kind` (`bullet`, `number`, or `none`, out of the list) at `level`, or each its own; or, with `by`, moved that many levels deeper (negative: shallower), from 0 to 8, a paragraph that is no item becoming a bullet as it goes deeper. Its `list` is written where it lives, as `choose` writes a property.

fork.description: Write it into `state`'s own props, wherever `list` lives now.

oneOf.description: One property of a node (`prop`: a property, or one key of an object property, `style/color`), as an inspector chooses it (ADR-0013): `value` is written where the property lives. A value written out where the theme has names (a color, a text size, a length in canvas units: lint W300's) goes in the deck's `overrides`, the only place it is legal, and so does any value where the overrides set the property, since they win in every state. Else it goes in the latest delta that sets it, from `state` back along what it tracks, else in the node's own; without `state`, in the node's own. `null` takes it away where it lives, so what is under it shows.

fork.description: Write it into `state`'s own props, wherever it lives now: it shows there, and in the states that track it as they take the rest of its props, and the others show what they did. Refused for a value that goes in the deck's `overrides`, which hold in every state.

oneOf.description: One of a chart's annotations (SPEC §3.7, PLAN 2.67), as the editor makes it from a mark: `annotation` added after the chart's others; or, with `index`, merged into the one at that place among them, what it gives replacing what that one has (`at` whole, and a `null` `text` or `role` taken away); or, `null` with `index`, that one taken away. The chart's `annotations` as `state` shows them are written where they live, as `choose` writes them; with `fork`, into `state`'s own props. An annotation must stand where its kind can, as validation says.

fork.description: Write the chart's annotations into `state`'s own props, wherever they live now: they show so there, and in the states that track it.

oneOf.description: A chart or a table reads the data source `data` (`q4` or `@q4`), in a state (a data update, morphed by key) or in its defaults. `source` declares it, or replaces it if the deck has it.

A theme preset. With `motion`, a motion preset becomes the node's `enter`, `exit`, or `emphasis`. Without, a shader takes a shader preset whole: the preset's kind, and none of its own `palette` or `params`, which would win over the preset's.

When a motion of `node`'s in `state` starts and how long it runs (PLAN 2.44): its `delay`, ms, and its `duration`, ms or a theme duration, each per unit, written where the motion is written. That is the state's choreography item that moves the node so, else the node's own preset or `anim` where it lives.
A state, `after` or `before` another, else last. With `beat`, it joins that beat's states.
A state, moved `after` or `before` another. A state in delta mode tracks from the state before it, wherever that is now.
A state, and its place in the spine's beats. The state after it tracks from the one before it. A state that others build on (`slide`) or track from (`from`) stays.
A state's id, everywhere it is used: the states that build on it or track from it, and the spine's beats.

One property of state `id`, as an inspector chooses it (PLAN 2.36): its `layout`, its `transition` or one key of it (`transition/ease`), its `hold`, or its `notes`. A layout tracks (SPEC §2.2), so it is written where it lives: in the latest state that sets it, from `id` back along what it tracks, and each state that takes it from there changes with it; in `id` where none sets it. The rest are `id`'s own. A transition that is a bare duration, or none, stays bare while its duration is all it sets, and becomes an object to take another key. `null` takes a value away where it lives: a layout taken away shows what is under it, and a transition left with nothing cuts.

fork.description: Write a layout into `id` itself, wherever it lives now: it shows there, and in the states that track `id`, and the others show what they did. The rest are `id`'s own with or without it.

oneOf.description: The deck's theme: a theme file in the bundle (`scaena theme --apply` copies one in), or a theme inline.

Spot.description: Where `place` puts a node: one placement, keyed as `at` keys it (SPEC §3.4). Cells (`col` and `row`, each 1-based and inclusive, either alone spanning its grid), a slot of the state's layout template (`in`), a `rect`, a grid container's `area`, or a stack's `index`; in its container, or in another (`parent`).

parent.description: The container the node goes into, or `null` for the canvas; unsaid, it stays in its own (PLAN 2.50).

in.description: A slot of the state's layout template, or `canvas` or `grid`.

rect.description: `[x, y, w, h]`, canvas units: on the canvas, an override (W301), or from a frame's padding edge.

Listing.description: What `list` makes paragraphs: items of a kind, or none.

Annotating.description: What `annotate` gives a chart's annotation (PLAN 2.67): a whole one, to add, with its `kind` and `at`; or, for the one at an `index`, what changes in it.

text.description: What it says; `null` takes it away.

role.description: Its text's role; `null` takes it away, leaving the theme's `charts.annotation.role`.

Motion.description: The motion a motion preset is for.

Timed.description: A motion `time_motion` times: a preset's, or `anim` tracks.

drift.description: In shorter sides of the rect.

angle.description: Degrees clockwise from up: a linear gradient's direction (180, the default, runs top to bottom), a conic one's start.

x.description: A radial or conic gradient's center across the rect, 0 to 1.

y.description: A radial or conic gradient's center down the rect, 0 to 1.

radius.description: A radial gradient's radius, in shorter sides of the rect.

speed.description: Degrees a second a linear or conic gradient turns.

octaves.description: Layers of finer noise over the first (fractal Brownian motion); 1 is plain simplex noise.

speed.description: How fast the field changes, in noise cycles a second.

contrast.description: How far the field spreads across the palette.

fps.description: How many times a second the grain changes; 0 holds it still.

size.description: A particle's radius, in shorter sides of the rect.

softness.description: How much of a particle's radius its edge fades over.

Format.description: Additional projections rendered from the same spine and nodes with other layout template sets.

ThemeRef.description: A theme file inside the bundle, or an inline theme object (schema: theme.schema.json).

SourceRef.description: A data file in the bundle, or rows inline.

Id.description: A slug: unique within its collection (SPEC §3.2).

Node.description: A node in the scene graph: its `type` and that type's properties. A node's type never changes across states (E104).

NodeProps.description: The properties every node type has (SPEC §3.3); each type adds its own.

alt.description: Accessible description; text nodes default to their content (SPEC §3.12).

formats.description: How it lays out in another of the deck's formats, by format (SPEC §3.4, ADR-0020): each property there takes the place of the node's own of the same name when the deck lays out in that format.

TextNode.description: Typographic text (SPEC §3.5): `text` or `runs`, set in a theme role.

style.description: What this node changes about its role's look (SPEC §3.6).

measure.description: Max line length in characters (overrides the role's).

list.description: Its paragraphs as a list's items (SPEC §3.5, ADR-0018): one entry for each paragraph a hard line break ends, in order, `null` for one that is no item. Paragraphs past its end are no items.

ShapeNode.description: Vector geometry: `path` (SVG path data) or a `kind`.

ImageNode.description: An image from the bundle, a PNG or a JPEG, placed in its box (SPEC §3.3).

src.description: The image file's path in the bundle; `assets/<sha256>.<ext>` once saved.

focal.description: The point of the image that lines up with the same point of the box, in fractions of the crop, as CSS `object-position`; default [0.5, 0.5].

crop.description: The part of the image to show, [x, y, w, h] in fractions of the image.

radius.description: Rounds the corners of what shows.

ChartNode.description: A data-bound chart (SPEC §3.7): a declarative spec compiled to marks.

orient.description: Which way a `bar`'s or a `stackedBar`'s bars run (PLAN 1.29): up from the baseline, the default, or across it, the categories down the side and their names read across. Any other kind is E106.

dataTransform.description: Steps run in order before the chart reads its data: filter, derive, sort, limit, aggregate, fold, pivot (SPEC §3.10; expressions in docs/spec/expr.md).

interval.description: A `range`'s interval about each value (PLAN 1.30): the fields that hold its low and high ends. Any other kind is E106.

facet.description: Small multiples (PLAN 1.31): a panel for each value of a field, on one shared scale, each named by its value.

projected.description: Which of a line's or an area's rows are a forecast or an estimate (PLAN 1.28).

key.description: The field that identifies a mark across states.

TableNode.description: A data-bound table (SPEC §3.3): rows from a data source, set in the theme's `tables` styles, each row matched by `key` across states.

dataTransform.description: Steps run in order before the table reads its data (SPEC §3.10).

columns.description: Its columns, in order; every column of the data when unset.

key.description: The field that identifies a row across states; the first column's when unset.

header.description: The header row, shown unless false.

ShaderNode.description: A parametric background or fill (SPEC §3.8): a kind, a seed, a theme palette, and typed params, its own or a theme preset's. No shader source, ever.

palette.description: A shader palette from the theme; the preset's when unset.

preset.description: A shader preset from the theme, of this kind: its palette and params are this node's, unless the node sets its own.

StackNode.description: A layout container along one axis (CSS flex, SPEC §3.4). Its children name it in `at.parent`.

axis.description: `y` (the default) stacks children top to bottom, `x` left to right.

distribute.description: Where leftover space along the axis goes: `start` (the default), `center`, `end`, or between and around the children.

radius.description: Rounds the corners of the container's `fill` and `stroke`.

GridNode.description: A layout container on a grid of its own (CSS grid, SPEC §3.4). Its children name it in `at.parent` and take an `area`, a `col`/`row` range, or the next free cell.

areas.description: Named areas, one string per row of cells, as CSS `grid-template-areas`: `["head head", "left right"]`; `.` leaves a cell unnamed.

radius.description: Rounds the corners of the container's `fill` and `stroke`.

FrameNode.description: A layout container whose children place themselves by `at.rect`, relative to its padding (SPEC §3.4). Its children name it in `at.parent`.

radius.description: Rounds the corners of the container's `fill` and `stroke`.

GroupNode.description: Nodes drawn together, each placed on the slide by its own `at` (SPEC §3.4). Its children name it in `at.parent`.

Semantic.description: Communicative function, independent of visual role (SPEC §3.3). Reserved for narrative lints; optional.

Color.description: Theme token name (e.g. "accent", "color.ink") or a literal (#rrggbb[aa], oklch(...)). Literals outside overrides are lint W300.

Length.description: A length in canvas units, a token reference (e.g. "space.4"), or a percentage string.

Clip.description: Clip to the node's box, or to SVG path data.

Placement.description: Where a node goes. One placement wins: `rect`, else `in`, else `col`/`row` (SPEC §3.4). Grid cells and slots are theme-managed; `rect` is an explicit override (lint W301 in template-managed states). In a container (`parent`), `col`/`row` and `area` are its grid's, `rect` is relative to a frame's padding, and a stack places its children itself.

in.description: Named slot in the state's layout template, or `canvas` or `grid`.

parent.description: The container this node is in: a `stack`, `grid`, `frame`, or `group` (ADR-0008).

index.description: Order among the container's children, as CSS `order`: ascending, default 0, ties in `nodes` order.

area.description: A named area of the grid container this node is in.

Range.description: A grid index or an inclusive [start, end] range (1-based).

Rect.description: [x, y, w, h] in canvas units.

Align.description: Alignment within a slot or cell. Vertical anchors include typographic ones (SPEC §3.4).

NodeTransition.description: How this node moves between two states that both show it (SPEC §3.9).

PresetRef.description: A theme motion preset by name, or a preset with parameters.

Duration.description: Milliseconds, or a named theme duration ("fast", "standard", "slow").

Easing.description: Named theme easing or a cubic Bézier [x1, y1, x2, y2].

Spring.description: Named theme spring or explicit parameters.

SplitUnit.description: What a choreographed entrance splits its target into.

LookParams.description: Numbers a look sets on what its unit draws.

progress.description: How much of each outline a shape strokes is drawn, from where the outline starts.

AnimTracks.description: Per-property keyframe tracks within a state, each property a look's (SPEC §3.9): `opacity`, `translate`, `scale`, `rotate`, and `progress`. They never track to the next state.

t.description: Milliseconds from the start of the track.

v.description: Value; its type must match the property.

FormatLayout.description: A node's layout in one of the deck's formats (SPEC §3.4, ADR-0020): where it goes, how big, how it is turned, a container's tracks and spacing, and a text's lines. Each property takes the place of the node's own of the same name in that format; a property its type does not have is E106, as anywhere on the node.

Padding.description: One length for every side, or 2–4 lengths CSS-style.

Tracks.description: A count of equal tracks, or each track's size.

TextStyle.description: What a text node, or a run, changes about its role's look (SPEC §3.6): the role's own properties, by name; each replaces the role's. `family` names a theme family and `color` a theme color token or role. A literal color, and any `size`, is a pixel value: theme-legal only in `overrides` (lint W300 elsewhere).

italic.description: Set in the family's italic face (SPEC §3.5), or, `false`, upright. None is synthesized: a family without one sets the text upright (lint W231).

leading.description: Line height as a multiple of size.

style.description: What this run changes about its role's look, after the node's `style` when the run is set in the node's role (SPEC §3.6).

link.description: Where the run goes when it is followed (SPEC §3.5, PLAN 2.70): a web address, or a state of the deck. It is drawn underlined.

quote.description: The value of a data source the run's text is (SPEC §3.5, ADR-0019, PLAN 2.72): its text is the figure as last set, which every write sets again from the data.

Link.description: Where a link goes (PLAN 2.70): a web address (`https:`, `http:`, or `mailto:`), which the player opens in a new window, or a state of the deck, which it shows.

Quote.description: A value of a data source that a run quotes (ADR-0019): a cell of the source, read as a chart reads it, through its `dataTransform`, written by `format`.

data.description: The source, as a chart names it: `@` and its id.

dataTransform.description: Steps the source is read through, as a chart's (SPEC §3.10).

row.description: The row: the one whose columns hold these values, or an index from 0, negative from the end (`-1`, the last). Without one, the table has one row.

column.description: The column whose cell it is.

format.description: How the cell is written: a number format for a number, a date format for a date (SPEC §3.7). Without one, as a chart writes a category.

anyOf.description: The one row whose columns hold these values.

QuoteKey.description: A value a quote's row is found by.

TextFit.description: What a text node does when its text does not fit (SPEC §3.4).

TextSplit.description: What a text node's own `split` divides it into for motion.

ListItem.description: A paragraph of a text as an item of a list (SPEC §3.5, ADR-0018): bulleted or numbered, at a level, 0 the outermost. Its marker and indent are the theme's (`type.lists`).

ImageFit.description: How an image meets its box.

oneOf.description: Fills the box, cutting what overflows (the default).
Fits inside the box, whole.
Stretched to the box.

ChartKind.description: v1 chart kinds (SPEC §3.7); waffle and heatmap are deferred. A `slope` compares two states, a line a series from the first to the second, both ends labeled and the change said; a `range` spans the value axis at each category, a dumbbell between its series or each value with its `interval` (PLAN 1.30).

ChartOrient.description: Which way a chart's bars run (SPEC §3.7, PLAN 1.29).

oneOf.description: Up from the baseline, the categories along the foot.
Across from the baseline, the categories down the side.

Encoding.description: One chart channel bound to a data field.

scale.description: Theme data palette name for color encodings (categorical | sequential | diverging).

Sort.description: A sort direction, or a field to sort by.

Interval.description: The fields that hold each value's interval on a `range` (SPEC §3.7, PLAN 1.30).

low.description: The field of its low end.

high.description: The field of its high end.

Facet.description: How a chart splits into small multiples (SPEC §3.7, PLAN 1.31).

field.description: The field whose values split the data, a panel each, in the order they first appear.

columns.description: How many panels stand in a row; unset, the count that makes each panel nearest 3:2.

Projected.description: Which of a line's or an area's rows are projected: a forecast, or an estimate (SPEC §3.7). The rows whose `field` holds `value`, or a true one when no value is given. The line runs dashed from the last actual point through them, the area under them is lighter, and their value labels say they are estimates.

value.description: What `field` holds in a projected row; `true` when unset.

note.description: What a projected value's label says after the value; the theme's `charts.projected.note` when unset.

collide.description: How labels that collide resolve (lint W310 otherwise).

LabelShow.description: Which values a chart prints. `auto` (the theme's `charts.label.show`, else by kind) puts the data on the marks: every bar, dot, and slice; a line's or an area's first and last; a scatter's none.

Legend.description: Where a chart's legend stands, alone or with a title (SPEC §3.7).

LegendPlace.description: Where a legend stands. `auto` is the theme's `charts.legend.place`, else `direct`. `direct` names each series at its end, beside the plot, where a chart has ends: a line, an area, or a stacked bar; any other chart places it `top`.

place.description: `top` when unset: a titled legend is a legend, not labels at the series' ends.

title.description: Printed before the entries, in the legend's role.

Annotation.description: A chart annotation (SPEC §3.7): a rule, a band, a callout, or a highlight, in the theme's `charts.annotation` style.

at.description: Where it stands, by kind: a rule at `x` or `y`, a band from one to another of either, a callout at `x` (and `y`, or a `series`), a highlight on categories `x` and series.

text.description: What it says; a highlight says nothing.

AnnotationAt.description: An annotation's place: a category or an x value (a number, or a date as ISO 8601), a value on the value axis, and a series, each one or several by kind.

Place.description: One value, or several: a band's two ends, or what a highlight picks out.

Scalar.description: A number, or text: a category, a series, or a date.

title.description: The header's text; the field's name when unset.

format.description: How its numbers or dates print (docs/spec/format.md).

align.description: Where its text sits across the column; `end` for numbers, else `start`, when unset.

ColumnAlign.description: Where a column's text sits across it.

ShaderParam.description: A shader parameter: a number, or a name its kind lists (a gradient's `shape`).

slide.description: The slide this state builds on: its first state's id. A state without one starts a slide named by its own id.

from.description: Track from this state instead of the previous one (branch).

layout.description: Layout template name from the theme.

props.description: Per-node property deltas for this state. Keys are node ids.

remove.description: Nodes that exit in this state.

hold.description: Auto-advance dwell in ms (video and kiosk).

StateMode.description: How a state relates to the one before it (SPEC §2.2).

oneOf.description: Declare changes only; unchanged properties track forward.
Everything explicit; nothing tracks.

Transition.description: The transition into a state: a bare duration, or the object form (SPEC §3.9). A state without one cuts.

StateDelta.description: The delta a state applies to one node: any node type's property, or null to delete it. An object value merges one level into the tracked one (the …Delta forms), so its keys are optional and null deletes one. An empty delta shows the node with its defaults (SPEC §2.2). Whether a property belongs to the node's type is checked on the resolved state (PLAN 1.2).

TransformDelta.description: `Transform` in a state's delta: it merges one level into the tracked value, so every key is optional and null deletes one (SPEC §2.2).

PaintDelta.description: `Paint` in a state's delta: a whole value, or an object that merges one level into the tracked one (SPEC §2.2).

SolidPaintDelta.description: `SolidPaint` in a state's delta: it merges one level into the tracked value, so every key is optional and null deletes one (SPEC §2.2).

GradientPaintDelta.description: `GradientPaint` in a state's delta: it merges one level into the tracked value, so every key is optional and null deletes one (SPEC §2.2).

StrokeDelta.description: `Stroke` in a state's delta: it merges one level into the tracked value, so every key is optional and null deletes one (SPEC §2.2).

PlacementDelta.description: `Placement` in a state's delta: it merges one level into the tracked value, so every key is optional and null deletes one (SPEC §2.2).

SizeDelta.description: `Size` in a state's delta: it merges one level into the tracked value, so every key is optional and null deletes one (SPEC §2.2).

AlignDelta.description: `Align` in a state's delta: a whole value, or an object that merges one level into the tracked one (SPEC §2.2).
